outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Large Language Models and the Need for Quantization
outline.description: Sets the stage by reviewing the rapid growth of LLMs, their computational demands, and why reducing precision is crucial for sustainability and deployment.
subtopics: Evolution of LLM size and capability
Energy and latency bottlenecks in modern transformer models
Overview of quantization: post‑training vs. training‑time quantization
Limitations of 4‑bit and higher‑bit quantization for large‑scale LLMs
Motivation for exploring extreme low‑bit regimes

outline.description: Introduces the original BitNet design, its computation paradigm, and the theoretical benefits of removing multiplications from matrix‑multiply operations.
subtopics: Review of traditional transformer arithmetic (FP16/BF16)
BitNet’s replacement of nn.Linear with BitLinear
Binary weight representation and integer‑only accumulation
Energy model for floating‑point vs. integer operations
Prior results and open questions from the original BitNet paper

outline.chapter_title: Design of BitNet b1.58 – A 1.58‑Bit Large Language Model
outline.description: Details the architectural modifications that turn BitNet into a ternary‑weight model, including quantization functions, activation handling, and integration with LLaMA components.
subtopics: Why ternary weights? Introducing the zero state
AbsMean quantization function for weights
Mathematical derivation of RoundClip and scaling factor γ
Activation quantization strategy (signed 8‑bit, removal of zero‑point)
Adopting LLaMA‑style components: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary embeddings, bias‑free design
Implementation notes for popular libraries (HuggingFace, vLLM, llama.cpp)
Training‑time considerations: optimizer, learning‑rate schedule, token budget

outline.description: Explains the experimental setup used to train BitNet b1.58 from scratch, including data sources, token counts, and scaling recipes.
subtopics: Dataset preparation – RedPajama and StableLM token recipes
Token budgets: 100 B vs. 2 T tokens
Hyper‑parameter choices for 3B, 7B, 13B, 70B models
Mixed‑precision training pipelines for ternary weights
Practical tips for stabilizing training with extreme quantization

outline.chapter_title: Performance Evaluation – Perplexity and Zero‑Shot Accuracy
outline.description: Presents the core empirical results comparing BitNet b1.58 to full‑precision LLaMA baselines across language modeling and downstream tasks.
subtopics: Perplexity benchmarks on WikiText‑2 and C4
Zero‑shot evaluation suite (ARC‑E, ARC‑C, Hellaswag, Winogrande, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BoolQ, etc.)
Interpretation of scaling trends: when does b1.58 match FP16?
Statistical significance and error analysis of the gaps
Effect of the additional zero weight on feature filtering

outline.chapter_title: Inference Efficiency – Memory, Latency, Throughput, and Energy
outline.description: Analyzes how ternary weights translate into practical gains on hardware, covering measurement methodology and results.
subtopics: GPU memory footprint comparison (FP16 vs. b1.58)
Latency per token using FasterTransformer and 2‑bit Ladder kernels
Throughput scaling with batch size and pipeline parallelism
Energy consumption model for matrix multiplication (INT8 addition vs. FP16 mul+add)
Empirical energy savings on 7 nm silicon estimates
Discussion of remaining overheads (embeddings, KV‑cache, non‑linearities)

outline.description: Derives and illustrates the observed trade‑off curves that relate model size, performance, and inference cost in the ternary regime.
subtopics: Empirical equivalence pairs (e.g., 13B b1.58 ≈ 3B FP16)
Formulation of a cost‑performance scaling law
Implications for model selection under a fixed budget
Limitations and open questions about extrapolation to larger models

outline.description: Explores how the ternary‑weight paradigm can be combined with other efficiency techniques and application scenarios.
subtopics: 1‑bit Mixture‑of‑Experts (MoE) – memory and communication benefits
Native long‑sequence support via low‑bit KV‑cache compression
Edge and mobile deployment: CPU friendliness, SRAM vs. DRAM trade‑offs
Potential for further activation compression (4‑bit, sub‑byte)
Case studies: on‑device QA, dialogue agents, and real‑time translation

outline.chapter_title: Hardware Implications and Future Processor Designs
outline.description: Discusses how the computation model of BitNet b1.58 invites new hardware architectures and what design choices would maximize its advantages.
subtopics: Review of existing LPU/GPUs optimized for low‑bit ops (e.g., Groq)
Design of integer‑add‑centric matrix units
Memory hierarchy optimizations for ternary weight storage
Co‑design of quantization kernels and systolic arrays
Research roadmap for ASICs dedicated to 1‑bit/1.58‑bit LLMs

outline.description: Summarizes the key takeaways, reflects on the broader impact of 1.58‑bit LLMs, and outlines promising directions for research and industry.
subtopics: Recap of performance‑cost parity with full‑precision models
Potential for democratizing large‑scale LLMs
Open challenges: training stability, mixed‑precision pipelines, benchmark standardization
Future research avenues: richer tokenization, adaptive quantization, synergy with sparsity
Ethical and environmental considerations of ultra‑efficient LLMs
